classification.classification_note: The reproduced write happens in `fuzz_reader_transmit`, but the source-level defect is in `fuzz_get_chunk`: returned chunk bytes are not consumed from the transcript state, so later transmits reuse overlapping bytes as new lengths, status words, and payloads that can outrun `cac_cac1_get_certificate`'s `len`-based bookkeeping.

bug_description.normalized: The `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` target stores the fuzz input as a fake smart-card transcript. In vulnerable `fuzz_get_chunk`, each call consumes only the two-byte header and returns a payload pointer without consuming the payload bytes, so later callbacks reinterpret overlapping transcript bytes as new chunk lengths, status words, and response payloads. During CAC certificate reading, `cac_cac1_get_certificate` requests at most `len` bytes per iteration but sets `apdu.resplen` to the whole remaining `left`; `fuzz_reader_transmit` then caps copies only against `apdu.resplen`, not `apdu.le`. One or more earlier overlapping responses therefore write more than the requested `len`, while the loop advances `out_ptr` and `left` only by `len`, and a later 30-byte transmit overflows the local stack `buf[CAC_MAX_SIZE]`, matching the saved ASan write.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled fuzz buffer as the fake reader transcript later consumed by `fuzz_get_chunk()`.
source.value_from: The staged 330-byte `poc` passed into `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; `fuzz_add_reader()` stores that raw buffer and its size in `reader->drv_data` for later reader callbacks.

sink.description: The fake-reader transmit callback performs the final 30-byte copy into the stale tracked tail of `cac_cac1_get_certificate`'s stack buffer, producing the witnessed stack-buffer-overflow write.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 30` at `fuzz_reader_transmit` line 129 and identifies `cac_cac1_get_certificate` line 68 (`buf`) as the overflown stack object.

root_cause.description: After choosing the current payload pointer, `fuzz_get_chunk` returns it without consuming `*chunk_size` bytes from the transcript state, so later calls reuse overlapping bytes as new fake APDU chunks.
root_cause.note: The real fix commit `3c87ffaa021ea53a84a2fe3977ecea945b4cc5b3` replaces this return block with a local `c_size`, then subtracts `c_size` from `data->Size` and advances `data->Data` by `c_size` before storing the outputs, so later callbacks cannot reopen the same payload bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: The libFuzzer-provided input buffer is handed to the project helper that creates the fake reader transcript state.

parser_admitted.description: Synthetic binding reached CAC certificate loading, so the fake reader transcript was accepted far enough to drive repeated certificate APDU reads into `cac_cac1_get_certificate`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, so this repair stayed source-grounded and cannot pin the earlier over-copy and the crashing transmit to exact transcript offsets, raw overlapping chunk lengths, or the number of intermediate reader callbacks between the explicit later `fuzz_get_chunk()` producer calls shown here.

The staged `patch.diff` artifact is commit `7a1e42e1352201127d1a97b6cb5f41e48cace0f5` (`fixed compiler warning`, OSS-Fuzz issue 18701) and does not explain the reproduced overflow. The causal patch grounding here comes from the metadata's declared `fixed_commit` (`3c87ffaa021ea53a84a2fe3977ecea945b4cc5b3`) and the local repository history.

coarse_trace.summary: The PoC is stored as the fake reader transcript state later consumed by `fuzz_get_chunk`.
An earlier reader callback consumes only a two-byte header and returns `data->Data` without consuming the payload, leaving the transcript cursor inside bytes it just exposed.
CAC certificate reading starts with `buf[CAC_MAX_SIZE]`, tracks `left` / `out_ptr`, and on each loop iteration sets `apdu.le = len` but `apdu.resplen = left`.
During an earlier certificate-read transmit, a later `fuzz_get_chunk` call reinterprets overlapping payload bytes as the response chunk that feeds the first over-copy.
That earlier overlapping response can copy more than the requested `len` because it caps only against `apdu.resplen`, not `apdu.le`.
The loop still advances `left` and `out_ptr` only by `len` and, on fake `0x63` status bytes, derives another `next_len`, leaving a stale tracked tail pointer.
A subsequent later `fuzz_get_chunk` call again reuses overlapping bytes to produce the response chunk for the crashing transmit.
The final transmit copies 30 bytes into the stale tail pointer and overflows `cac_cac1_get_certificate`'s stack `buf` exactly as ASan reports.

fine_trace.note: Stores the staged 330-byte PoC as the fake reader transcript. Every later `fuzz_get_chunk()` call reads chunk headers and payload pointers from this saved `data->Data` / `data->Size` state.

On a preceding reader callback, these lines consume only the two-byte chunk header from the stored transcript: `data->Size` shrinks by 2, `data->Data` advances by 2, and `*chunk_size` comes from only the first header byte. The cursor now points at the start of the would-be payload region.

Root cause. The same call returns `data->Data` as the chunk and clamps the length, but it never subtracts `*chunk_size` from `data->Size` or advances `data->Data` past the returned payload bytes. The reader state therefore remains positioned inside bytes it already exposed, so later callbacks reinterpret overlapping payload bytes as new chunk headers, status words, and response payloads.

On the saved crash path, whose reachability through `sc_pkcs15emu_cac_init` is recorded separately, certificate reading starts with a fixed 4096-byte stack buffer, `left = 4096`, `out_ptr = buf`, and `next_len = MIN(left, 100)`.

fine_trace.var: len, out_ptr, left, apdu.resp, apdu.le, apdu.resplen
fine_trace.note: On an earlier certificate-read iteration, the caller requests only `len = next_len` bytes from the reader but publishes the whole remaining `left` as `apdu.resplen` and the current tracked tail `out_ptr` as the destination.

During the later `fuzz_get_chunk()` call that feeds the first over-copy transmit, the same header-only parse runs again while the transcript state still points inside bytes previously returned because step 2 never consumed them. Two overlapping bytes become a fresh chunk header and the cursor advances only past those two bytes.

This later `fuzz_get_chunk()` call returns an overlapping payload pointer from that reused region and again leaves the payload bytes unconsumed. Its `chunk` / `chunk_size` outputs feed the earlier over-copy transmit.

The earlier overlapping response uses its last two bytes as `SW1` / `SW2`, then reduces `chunk_size` by 2. The remaining candidate payload length still comes entirely from overlapping transcript bytes, not from the caller's requested `len`.

On the vulnerability path, some earlier transmit reaches this statement with an overlapping payload longer than the requested `len`; the code then copies `apdu->resplen > len` bytes because it caps only against `apdu->resplen`, not `apdu->le`. This is the only source location that can create the stale tail consumed at the crash.

fine_trace.code: for (; left > 0; left -= len, out_ptr += len) {
fine_trace.note: The loop bookkeeping still records only `len` bytes as consumed. After step 8 over-copies beyond `len`, `left` stays too large and `out_ptr` lags behind the true filled end of `buf` by the earlier over-copy delta.

The loop reaches another iteration only while the earlier overlapping status bytes satisfy `apdu.sw1 == 0x63 && apdu.sw2 >= 1`; then `next_len` is derived from `apdu.sw2` while the stale bookkeeping from step 9 persists.

fine_trace.var: len, out_ptr, left, apdu.resp, apdu.le, apdu.resplen
fine_trace.note: On the later crashing iteration, the caller reuses the stale tracked tail as `apdu.resp`, requests only `len = next_len` bytes, and again exposes the whole stale `left` as `apdu.resplen`.

During the later `fuzz_get_chunk()` call that feeds the crashing transmit, the same header-only parse runs again while the vulnerable transcript state still points inside previously returned bytes. Another pair of overlapping bytes becomes the header for the crash response chunk.

This later `fuzz_get_chunk()` call returns the overlapping payload pointer for the crashing response and again leaves those bytes unconsumed. Its `chunk` / `chunk_size` outputs feed the crashing transmit.

On the crashing call, the overlapping response again strips its last two bytes into `SW1` / `SW2`, reduces `chunk_size` by 2, and optionally clamps `apdu->resplen` to that value. The saved artifacts prove only the result that `apdu->resplen` is 30 when the sink runs, not the raw overlapping chunk length or whether line 125 performed the final assignment.

Sink. `memcpy` writes 30 bytes from the later overlapping response into the stale destination pointer from step 11. ASan reports this exact statement as `WRITE of size 30` and identifies `cac_cac1_get_certificate`'s local `buf` at line 68 as the overflown stack object.

poc.trigger: The staged 330-byte PoC is consumed as a fake reader transcript. Under vulnerable `fuzz_get_chunk`, later reader callbacks reuse overlapping transcript bytes as new APDU responses; on the witnessed CAC certificate-read path, at least one earlier response writes more than the requested `len`, the loop advances `left` / `out_ptr` only by `len`, and a later transmit performs the saved 30-byte overflow copy into `buf[CAC_MAX_SIZE]`.

format.name: fuzz_pkcs15_reader fake-reader transcript
format.contract: A 330-byte `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` fake-reader transcript that reaches CAC certificate reading and, because `fuzz_get_chunk` does not consume returned payload bytes, causes at least one earlier overlapping response to copy more than the requested `len` while `cac_cac1_get_certificate` advances `left` / `out_ptr` only by `len`, after which a later transmit performs the observed 30-byte `memcpy(apdu->resp, chunk, apdu->resplen)` into the stale tail of `buf[CAC_MAX_SIZE]`.
